ov: A common name for frogs with short legs and dry, warty skin, especially the true toads. The “warts” are glands, and it’s a myth that handling a toad gives you warts.

why.dg: Glands behind the head hold a poison the toad releases when stressed. Some, like the cane toad, are much more toxic than others.
why.h: Toads living on land in cold regions dig a burrow and hibernate through winter.
why.ac: The common toad hides by day and comes out at dusk to hunt through the night.

rg: True toads are native to every continent except Australia and Antarctica.
df: Insects and other small invertebrates, hunted at night. The common toad will snap at almost any small, dark, moving object.

cf.tip: Toads are frogs with drier, rougher, wartier skin that live more on land. The split is informal and doesn’t match scientific classification.

fx: The common toad usually gets about by walking slowly or making short, shuffling jumps.
